rationale: M59.A7 (#825) cpp line-attribution round. Before it the analyzer emitted NO `line_number` on any row: the Calls and Instantiates rows carried only a `metadata.line` mirror and everything else carried nothing, so a member read reached the graph at line 0 (#870, the fmt lane) and 'jump to the call site' had no line. The contract that was landed (mirroring the C lane's #825 round) is one line per row, naming the node that NAMES the relationship, 1-based (R6), with the #873 mirror repeating that same value. The fixture pins the four shapes where the obvious node is the wrong one, all read off this file's own text: (1) a call takes the CALLEE LEAF — `callMultiLine`'s receiver ends on L33 while `size` is written on L34, so a row stamped with the call node would name L33; (2) `new` takes the CONSTRUCTED TYPE — the keyword is on L38 and `Widget()` on L39; (3) a member read takes the FIELD LEAF (L44) — the row that carried no line at all before this round, pinned by forbidding the `line_number: null` state rather than only asserting a number; (4) a `contains` takes the CHILD's own line (L25) so it can never disagree with the symbol range it mirrors, and an include takes its WRITTEN PATH (L22). Each forbid entry states a pre-fix value, so a revert of the node choice or of the base is a fixture failure rather than a silent drift.  M14 ONTOLOGY (2026-10-04): `#include` is C++'s FILE INCLUSION and is now a first-class `imports` edge — the same kind, with the same metadata, the C lane already emits for the identical construct (pinned there by c/macro-composed-include, reverted there by the `c/include-kind-downgraded` mutant). The measured reason: the one consumer that answers "what does this module depend on" is the LSP usages file-level section, which filters on `relationship_type IN ('imports','exports')` (src/lsp/graph_request.ts, src/lsp/graph_usages.ts), so a C++ include was invisible to it no matter what its metadata said. A LABEL move, not an edge move — 5,404 include sites in 905 corpus files, 5,118 distinct module names, and the include-dependency row count is identical before and after. Every row is still asserted with its line, its metadata and (where pinned) its exact count, and the `references` label is FORBIDDEN so a downgrade fails the fixture rather than only moving a number in a census. A `using`-dependency row stays `references`: an include dependency and a using-dependency are two facts, and only the first is file inclusion.
